messages:
raj: Heads up — terraform apply is stuck importing eu-gpu-pool, CI shows 'Acquiring state lock' since 2026-03-14 11:03 UTC. Pipeline: https://ci.redwood.dev/runs/1248
ops-bot: terraform apply failed: lock held by session 9734... created 2026-03-14T11:03:12Z; lock table: tf-locks (dynamodb)
mia: I saw this earlier this week. Usually a stale DynamoDB lease. Can someone check the LockID 'eu/gpu-pool/terraform.tfstate' in tf-locks?
kai: checking now, 1 min
kai: output:
```
aws dynamodb get-item --table-name tf-locks --key '{"LockID":{"S":"eu/gpu-pool/terraform.tfstate"}}'
# Item: { LockID: ..., Info: "{\"Operation\":\"Import\",\"ID\":\"9734\"}", TTL: 1700000000 }
```
raj: Before we force-unlock: confirm no active applies (Atlantis/GHA) and snapshot the state. If force-unlock and there's a mid-apply, we can corrupt state.
mia: confirmed no active Atlantis applies; CI run 1248 was cancelled. S3 has a version at 2026-03-14T11:02:45Z and then lock created at 11:03. TTL is already expired.
kai: saving a snapshot:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-terraform-eu/eu-gpu-pool/terraform.tfstate backups/eu-gpu-pool/1785123456.tfstate
```
then:
```
terraform force-unlock 9734
```
ops-bot: :warning: force-unlock performed by kai at 2026-03-14T11:07:00Z. Reminder: force-unlock will NOT undo partial state changes.
sarah: Can we add a lightweight CI guard that detects locks older than 15m and fails fast with a link to the lock owner instead of letting job sit?
raj: +1. I'll file an eng-infra ticket and add the guard to the terraform CI job. Ticket: https://go.redwood/issue/INFRA-482
mia: I'll follow up with a short runbook and add it to the runbooks page.
